prize_parts.citation: For the discovery that liquid-liquid phase separation and multivalent molecular interactions organize the cell into membraneless compartments

statement.case_for: Phase separation gives a clear underlying principle: demixing, surface tension and multivalency explain how cells organize their chemistry without membranes. The 2009 P-granule droplet work (Brangwynne, Hyman) is a sharp, dated origin, and Rosen's 2012 reconstitution showed that multivalent interactions are sufficient to drive it, so the original discovery separates cleanly from later refinements. The concept has generated work on signalling, neurodegeneration, gene regulation and condensate-targeting chemistry, which is the generative reach I look for. It is the one field with substantial support across the committee (four top-three rankings, five members ranking it), and a three-person citation can be explained to a broad audience.
statement.case_against: Physiological relevance is still argued case by case. Overexpression artefacts, the line between true phase separation and other assemblies, and thin in vivo evidence remain open, and there is no therapeutic payoff yet. The three-person cap also forces an uncomfortable exclusion of Pappu and Mittag, whose sequence-grammar work is quantitatively the most physical part of the field. If the committee judges the field too contested, B068 or B023 would be the safer prizes.

responses.point: Condensates are a young field with debated physiological relevance, so recognition may be premature.
responses.response: I take this seriously, and it is why I moved B003 to my preferred slot only after weighing it against B068. But the prize here would reward a physical-chemical discovery, that proteins and RNA demix into liquid compartments and that multivalency drives this, not every biological claim made since. That core has been reproduced in many independent labs for over a decade. The overreach concerns individual condensates in vivo, and the citation can be worded to avoid asserting it.

responses.point: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation make the concept stable and recognition timely.
responses.response: I agree on the origin and on Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen, but I would not call the concept settled. Several in vivo claims fail when concentrations are not physiological, and I want you to say plainly which results hold up. If you can show the core is separable from the contested claims, I think we can defend timeliness. If not, I would hold B003 less firmly.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B068) is a new modality that reaches undruggable targets, and PROTACs and molecular glues should be seen as one idea.
responses.response: I ranked B068 fourth, not low, and the chemical principle is real. My reservation is that I see two discoveries here: heterobifunctional PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli) and monovalent glues such as thalidomide and cereblon (Handa, Ito and others). The three-person trio covers the first and leaves out the second, and no PROTAC drug is approved yet. I am not persuaded that these belong in one citation, and I would like to see how you justify that.

responses.point: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics (B023) is an unambiguous two-person attribution that is overdue, with precedent from 2013 and 2024.
responses.response: This is my own opening first choice, and your point about attribution and maturity is the strongest argument for it. I put it below B003 because the two recent computational prizes may make the committee feel it has covered the area, and the case rests on impact in condensed-phase and materials simulation as much as in chemistry. I keep it as an alternative and would support it if the committee wants a mature, uncontested choice.

responses.point: Dye-sensitized solar cells (B033) are an overdue, extensively reproduced two-person invention.
responses.response: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel paper is a clean attribution, and I ranked B033 fifth. My concern is capability: the architecture mostly mattered for what it led to (perovskites) and I do not see the same unforeseen-opportunity argument now that commercial efficiency is limited. I would like to hear more about its lasting independent impact.

uncertainties: Whether the core physical-chemical discovery can be separated from contested in vivo claims about condensates
Whether Rosen or Pappu/Mittag deserves the third place
Whether B068 should be treated as one prize for PROTACs and molecular glues or split
Whether recent computational prizes lessen the case for B023
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Lund colleague of Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr, but none of the shortlisted candidates is connected to Lund in my profile.
